Why this matters now

Being very good at your work does not make you a good manager. Most people are promoted into it anyway: in a 2024 survey, 66% of managers had no formal training for the role. The good news is that leading people can be learned. A review of 335 studies found that leadership training works.

Being human is extraordinary, and in the AI era it matters more than ever.

Mean-tering™

One short English word. Three meanings. Each one is a part of the method.

mean /miːn/

  1. adjective

    Unkind. Cruel. Small.

    The first job is to take meanness out of delivery: the blame, the public shaming, the quiet fear before every steering meeting. Not by ignoring it, but by understanding what sits behind it. Usually it is pressure, or fear, or a person who was never taught another way. Fear can look like power. It is not power. It is frustration.

    In a session: “Who in this chapter is being mean, and what are they afraid of?”

  2. noun, as in meaning

    What it is for.

    Teams deliver numbers: dates, budgets, story points, percentages. The second question is what those numbers really deliver, and to whom. When people see the meaning of the work, the numbers usually follow. When they only see the numbers, people start to hide the truth behind them.

    In a session: “If this project is a success, what changes for a real person?”

  3. verb, as in what does it mean?

    The logic behind the request.

    Every method asks for artefacts: a status report, a risk log, a sign-off, a sprint review. The name of the method matters less than the logic behind each artefact. Why does it exist? What question should it answer? When a team understands that, a report stops being theatre and starts being useful again.

    In a session: “What is this status report supposed to tell us that we did not already know?”

Under all three meanings is one belief: there is light in every person. We work from facts, we separate them from interpretations, and we look for the human being behind the role.

Programs for teams: three sizes, one story

Your teams read one business novel, The Friday We Promised. Then they talk about their own projects with more facts and less fear. About Cris

Cris Calin has led people for close to twenty years, in the high-pressure world of technology delivery. She co-founded Evolvance in 2026 to bring what she learned in delivery rooms to the people who lead them.

  • Close to twenty years of leading people and teams through high-pressure delivery.
  • Has led and worked with people from Europe, the US, India and Asia (Romanian, Polish, American, Indian, Japanese citizens, etc.).
  • English and French at C1 level. Romanian is her native language.
  • Volunteer in financial education for young people with various organisations since 2016.

She does not believe AI will take our jobs. She also does not believe people are hired only to deliver. Many leaders were good at doing the work and were then promoted, without anyone explaining what a leader is. Mean-tering™ is her attempt to explain it, in plain words.
